content:
monitor-bot: ALERT: sudden rise in tool-invoke latency and structured-output error % on prod-rwd-gpu-us-east-1. fncall failures 4.3x baseline, queue depth spiking. paging @sara-nguyen @kevin-wu — dashboard: https://telemetry.redwood/alerts/2367890123 :rotating_light:

sara-nguyen: acked. I'm on it, pulling logs now. which tenant slices are seeing highest error rates?

kevin-wu: i'm awake, grabbing topology map. looks like a handful of high-fanout tenants + some free-tier bursts.

irina-kovacs: saw structured-output JSON marshalling timeouts in the agg logs — heavy CPU on converter workers. might be a downstream bottleneck not GPU.

eli-martin: +1 saw increased 429s from toolgateway and retry storms. suggests we need short-term gating.

sara-nguyen: decision call: do a staged mitigation. 1) soft-defer tool invocations for non-SLA tenants (queue, don't execute). 2) apply rolling cap on concurrent tool calls per host. 3) fallback structured-output to compact text for all tenants. inform support.

kevin-wu: agree. prefer to avoid outright disabling for dedicated customers. plan: target tag "tier:free" and tag "bot-heavy" first, then expand if needed.

oncall-runbook-bot: RUNBOOK STEP: apply tenant-scoped invoke-mode=defer -> use rwdctl or console toggle. If metrics improve, widen scope after 5m.

sara-nguyen: quick commands — I'll run them and paste logs.

sara-nguyen: ```bash
# soft-defer free tier tool calls
rwdctl config set --scope "tenant.tag:tier=free" --path tool_invocation.mode defer --reason "emergency backpressure"
# cap concurrent invocations per-host to 8
rwdctl runtime set --path concurrency.max_tool_calls 8 --hosts "rwd-prod-gpu-us-east-1"
```

eli-martin: running the console toggle for structured-output fallback to compact-text now.

eli-martin: ```json
{"action":"set_fallback","scope":"global","param":"structured_output.mode","value":"compact_text"}
```

monitor-bot: ACTION: tool_invocation.mode=defer applied for tenant.tag:tier=free. concurrency.max_tool_calls -> 8 on hosts: rwd-prod-gpu-us-east-1. structured_output.mode=compact_text set globally.

support-alex: notifying support team and drafting customer-safe message for affected non-enterprise customers. will post to zendesk and status page in ~10m if impact persists.

kevin-wu: check for backlog explosion — deferring means queued requests could pile up. we should enable short TTL for queued tool calls TTL=30s.

sara-nguyen: good call. setting queue_ttl and queue_consume_rate.

sara-nguyen: ```bash
rwdctl config set --scope "tenant.tag:tier=free" --path tool_invocation.queue_ttl 30s
rwdctl config set --scope "tenant.tag:tier=free" --path tool_invocation.queue_drain_rate 50/s
```

irina-kovacs: monitoring converters — compact_text reduced CPU by ~40% on a sample host. looking good.

monitor-bot: METRIC SNAPSHOT (t+60s): fncall errors down 28%, 429s down 35%, tool gateway latency median -18%. queue depth decreased after TTL enforcement.

support-alex: posted preliminary note to status: "We are observing elevated errors on tool-based features for non-enterprise accounts. We are applying mitigations to reduce impact. If you see continued failures please contact support." (internal link: https://status.redwood/incident/2367890123)

kevin-wu: moving to rolling expansion: if metrics hold steady for next 5m, we'll include low-commit enterprise tenants tagged 'trial' but with stricter rate (0.2 rps). plan documented below.

sara-nguyen: creating a rateplan for trial tenants now.

sara-nguyen: ```bash
rwdctl rate-limit set --scope "tenant.tag:trial=true" --fncall-rps 0.2 --burst 2 --reason "mitigation"
```

eli-martin: I'm watching host-level CPU and tool gateway queue consumers. so far no host OOM or long GC.

monitor-bot: METRIC SNAPSHOT (t+5m): error rate down 48% vs peak, overall QPS reduced 22%. structured-output payloads trimmed significantly.

kevin-wu: good. i'll stay on this for the next handoff. sara, can you draft a brief for the morning incident review describing triggers + root hypothesis (converter CPU + bursty retries) and mitigation timeline?

sara-nguyen: will do. also capture the exact config diffs: tool_invocation.mode changes, TTL, rate limits, concurrency cap.

support-alex: customer impact tracker updated. affected customers: free-tier bulk apps (list attached in support doc). outreach scheduled for enterprise trial customers in 15m.

oncall-runbook-bot: REMINDER: if mitigation extends beyond 1h, create a customer-facing incident update and notify legal for any contract exposure.

irina-kovacs: during cleanup we should add a small exp backoff on client retries to avoid a synchronized surge when we lift caps. recommend server-suggested Retry-After header set to 2s for affected tenants.

sara-nguyen: applied Retry-After header for deferred tenants.

monitor-bot: STATS (t+12m): continued improvement. current error rate 19% over baseline (from 430% peak). queue depth baseline.

kevin-wu: handing off active pager to @kevin-wu (self) for next 30m while i coordinate postmortem draft. sara, push any remaining notes to the incident doc and pin. i'll update oncall channel in 15m with status.

sara-nguyen: noted. filing postmortem skeleton now.

kevin-wu: if we see another spike, fallback plan B is to fully disable structured-output for all non-SLA tenants and shift them to a read-only mode for tool features. prefer to avoid but it's ready.

support-alex: once we normalize please prepare a customer post-incident message with timeline and what we changed to mitigate. I'll coordinate approvals.

monitor-bot: CLOSE LOOP: at t+30m metrics stable, mitigation will be eased starting with trial tag -> raise rps to 0.5, then after 10m re-evaluate. scheduled rollback steps documented.

sara-nguyen: starting gradual rollback for trial tag to rps=0.5.

sara-nguyen: ```bash
rwdctl rate-limit set --scope "tenant.tag:trial=true" --fncall-rps 0.5 --burst 5 --reason "rollback step 1"
```

monitor-bot: final snapshot (t+45m): errors within 10% of baseline, tool gateway latencies stable. mitigation considered successful. recommend postmortem with root cause: converter CPU + retry amplification + lack of tenant-level soft-gating.

kevin-wu: thanks team. leaving notes for sla teams and ops to consider a permanent soft-defer mode for bursty tenants. handing off to next oncall @irina-kovacs in 15m. good job. :thumbsup:
